# Anuruddha Saṁyutta (SN 52)

**ID:** SN 52
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Anuruddha Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anuruddha Saṁyutta* (SN 52) is the fifty-second section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the *Mahāvagga* and comprising twenty-four discourses arranged in two chapters (*vagga*s) [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. While the Venerable Anuruddha is traditionally renowned for clairvoyance and spiritual attainments, this collection consistently presents him as an ardent exponent of mindfulness meditation (*satipaṭṭhāna*), which figures explicitly in every discourse [Gethin 2001; Bodhi 2003]. Throughout the samyutta, Anuruddha attributes his cultivation of spiritual knowledges, absorptions, and supernormal powers—such as the "power of the noble ones" (*ariya-iddhi*), the divine eye, and the destruction of the taints—to the development of the four establishments of mindfulness (e.g., SN 52.1, SN 52.15–24) [Bodhi 2003; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. Several discourses depict Anuruddha explaining to fellow monks how *satipaṭṭhāna* enables one to endure severe bodily illness with serenity (SN 52.10), forms the habitual dwelling of both trainees and arahants (SN 52.4–5, SN 52.9), and leads steadily to the destruction of craving (SN 52.7) [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Anālayo 2018; Wen 2011].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- This file contains 8 suttas; 8 of them have known parallels. Full parallels by collection: SĀ (4), Pali (1)
- Examples of full non-Pali parallels: sn52.4-5 ↔ SĀ 542-543; SN 52.6 Tatiyakaṇḍakīsutta ↔ SA 537 松林; SN 52.10 Bāḷhagilānasutta ↔ SA 541 所患; SN 52.23 Dibbacakkhusutta ↔ SA 539 松林

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha (2003) — Noted structure, role as appendix to SN 47, formulaic combinations in SN 52.1, and powers claimed through satipaṭṭhāna.
- [Gethin 2001] Rupert Gethin, The Buddhist Path to Awakening (2001) — Discussed context in the Mahāvagga and consistent association with satipaṭṭhāna in every sutta.
- [Nyanaponika et al. 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha (2003) — Detailed specific suttas (SN 52.1, 52.2, 52.7, 52.9, 52.10, 52.15–24) and their doctrinal themes.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Confirmed two-chapter division and core theme of Anuruddha's satipaṭṭhāna practice.
- [Anālayo 2018] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Satipaṭṭhāna Meditation: A Practice Guide (2018) — Discussed SN 52.10 regarding mindfulness used to face severe illness.
- [Wen 2011] Tzungkuen Wen, A Study of Sukkhavipassaka in Pāli Buddhism — Discussed trainee/arahant practices (SN 52.4–5, SN 52.9), bearing pain (SN 52.10), and contrast between Pali supernormal powers and Chinese divine eye.
